statistics.locator: Results, paragraph on the after-effect phase (pointing, no visual feedback)
statistics.quote: ANOVA yielded significant effects for Episode (F(4,88)=66.84, P<0.001) and the interaction (F(4,88)=3.95, P<0.01); indeed a close look at Fig. 1 reveals that the after-effect declined somewhat faster in the young group.
statistics.admissible_reason: Within-participant main effect of Episode (practice/decline across after-effect episodes), not a between-group comparison of old vs young.
statistics.notes: This is the within-factor Episode effect from the ANOVA on the five after-effect episodes.

statistics.locator: Results, paragraph on the after-effect phase (pointing, no visual feedback)
statistics.quote: ANOVA yielded significant effects for Episode (F(4,88)=66.84, P<0.001) and the interaction (F(4,88)=3.95, P<0.01); indeed a close look at Fig. 1 reveals that the after-effect declined somewhat faster in the young group.
statistics.direction_quote: indeed a close look at Fig. 1 reveals that the after-effect declined somewhat faster in the young group
statistics.admissible_reason: Interaction term (Age × Episode), not a main between-group contrast on the after-effect magnitude.
statistics.notes: The paper interprets the interaction as a faster decline of the after-effect in the young group, not as a difference in overall after-effect magnitude.

statistics.locator: Results, paragraph on the after-effect phase
statistics.effect_as_written: Age (main effect) for the after-effect phase
statistics.direction_quote: the resulting after-effect was similar in both age groups, and gradually declined with practice; this age-independence is in marked contrast with the findings during adaptation
statistics.admissible_reason: No numerical statistic for the between-group (Age) effect on the after-effect is printed; the text only states the after-effect was similar in both age groups.
statistics.notes: For the after-effect ANOVA the paper lists only Episode and the interaction as significant; no F or p value is given for the Age main effect, so no between-group test statistic can be transcribed. Other F values on this page (Age F(1,22)=7.58 for the adaptation phase; Age F(1,22)=13.42 and F(1,22)=13.78 for the refresh phase; Procedure F(1,43)=144,09 for tracking transfer) belong to different phases/measures.

statistics.admissible_reason: No standardised effect size is printed anywhere on these pages.
statistics.notes: These pages report only F and t statistics with P values, plus exponential fit parameters for the adaptation curves; no d, g, or eta-squared values and no confidence intervals.

parsed.notes: The only after-effect statistics on page 3 come from one ANOVA on the five no-feedback after-effect episodes: Episode F(4,88)=66.84, P<0.001 and the interaction F(4,88)=3.95, P<0.01. The Age main effect is described verbally as absent ('the resulting after-effect was similar in both age groups ... this age-independence is in marked contrast with the findings during adaptation') but no number is printed for it, so no admissible between-group statistic exists for this outcome on these pages. Group means/SDs for the after-effect episodes appear only in Fig. 1 (figure, not text).
